videoStudio.composer.unreachable: Server unreachable. Is the backend running?
videoStudio.duration.chained: This clip is longer than {0}, the length of a run at best: it will be made of at least {1} runs generated one after the other, each starting from the last frame of the previous one. The real length of the runs follows this machine's memory: short for the first try of a model, then adjusted from what was measured. The time is multiplied and the motion can change from one run to the next.
videoStudio.duration.limit.model: Maximum {0}: the length this model is built for. Beyond it, the motion loses coherence and both memory and time explode.
videoStudio.duration.limit.chain: Maximum {0}: beyond it, the chained runs drift (the subject deforms, the motion repeats) and generation takes unreasonably long.
videoStudio.duration.steps: The model computes clips in steps: actual duration ≈ {0}.
videoStudio.duration.title: Duration
videoStudio.footer.menu.asSource: Use the clip as the source video
videoStudio.footer.menu.asSourceN: Use clip {0} as the source video
videoStudio.footer.menu.downloadLightN: Download clip {0} as a light version
videoStudio.footer.menu.lastFrameN: Last frame of clip {0} as the start
videoStudio.footer.reuse: Reuse these settings in the composer
videoStudio.footer.sameSeeds.hint: Runs again with the same seeds: gives the same clip again. Useful after changing a setting to judge its effect alone.
videoStudio.footer.vary.body: Runs the same prompt again with new random seeds: each try gives a different clip.
videoStudio.footer.vary.title: New variants (random seeds)
videoStudio.format.title: Format
videoStudio.help.aspect.body: Shape of the video: 16:9 landscape, 9:16 vertical, 1:1 square… The number of pixels stays close to the chosen definition; only the shape changes.
videoStudio.help.aspect.title: Format
videoStudio.help.attach.body: Click, drag and drop, or paste (⌘V). The slots above the prompt show what the model accepts: start image, end image, source video. A file dropped on a given slot goes there; otherwise it is placed automatically.
videoStudio.help.attach.title: Attach an image or a video
videoStudio.help.count.body: How many videos to generate for this prompt (different seeds). A video takes time and memory: each clip is computed one after the other, so 2 clips = twice the wait.
videoStudio.help.count.title: Number of clips
videoStudio.help.resolution.body: Size of the image in pixels (480p, 720p…). This is the most expensive setting: 720p needs ~2.25 times more computation than 480p. Models are trained at certain native sizes; below that, quality collapses (especially with Wan), and above it coherence may degrade.
videoStudio.help.resolution.tip: validate in 480p, then redo it in 720p with the same seed if you like the result.
videoStudio.help.resolution.title: Definition
videoStudio.help.seconds.body: Length of the video. The model computes a number of frames in steps (n × step + 1): the duration shown is rounded to the nearest real value. The longer the clip, the more memory and time explode: doubling the duration more than doubles the wait, and the movement becomes less coherent.
videoStudio.help.seconds.tip: start with short clips (2 to 4 s) to validate the idea.
videoStudio.help.seconds.title: Clip duration
videoStudio.help.slot.end.body: The video ends on this image: the model invents the transition between the start image and this one ("first/last frame"). It requires the start image, and only exists on some models.
videoStudio.help.slot.role.reference: Here it is a reference (subject, style), not the first frame.
videoStudio.help.slot.source.body: An existing video that the model edits following your prompt (change the mood, an object, the style…) while keeping its movement. Only for editing models.
videoStudio.help.slot.source.tip: the "Video influence" setting controls how much is transformed.
videoStudio.help.slot.start.body: The video starts from this image (image → video): the model animates it following your prompt, which should describe the movement rather than the image. Depending on the model, it is required, optional or ignored. For some models it is a plain "reference" image that inspires the subject without being the first frame.
videoStudio.help.slot.status.end.none: This model does not use it.
videoStudio.help.slot.status.end.optiona: Optional for this model (with the start image).
videoStudio.help.slot.status.source.none: This model cannot edit a video.
videoStudio.help.slot.status.start.none: This model does not use it.
videoStudio.help.slot.status.start.optio: Optional for this model: without it, the video starts from your text alone.
videoStudio.home.subtitle: Describe a scene, animate an image, or drop a video to edit it. Everything is computed on this machine.
videoStudio.import.ignoredSome: Some files were ignored: only images and videos are accepted.
videoStudio.import.oneVideo: Only one source video at a time: the first one is kept.
videoStudio.import.twoImages: Only two images (start and end) are used.
videoStudio.notice.endIgnored: {0} does not use an end image: it will be ignored.
videoStudio.notice.endWithoutStart: Add the start image too: the end image alone is not enough.
videoStudio.notice.english: {0} mostly understands English: write the prompt in English for a better result.
videoStudio.notice.needSource: {0} edits an existing video: add the source video to edit.
videoStudio.notice.needStart: {0} starts from an image: add the start image.
videoStudio.notice.sourceIgnored: {0} cannot edit a video: the source video will be ignored.
videoStudio.notice.startIgnored: {0} does not use a start image: it will be ignored.

videoStudio.prompt.placeholder.start: Describe the movement from the image… (action, camera, mood)
videoStudio.prompt.placeholder.text: Describe the scene to film… (subject, action, camera movement, light)
